prompt: Find the value of $2+2\times3^2$.
Determine the value of $\dfrac{1\times13\times13\times12}{1+13+13+12}$.

solutions.title: Simplify
solutions.body:
The numerator is $13\cdot13\cdot12=2028$ and the denominator is $1+13+13+12=39=3\cdot13$. So the value is $\frac{13\cdot13\cdot12}{3\cdot13}=13\cdot4=52$.

**Answer: 52**

prompt: Jess is standing in a queue of people. She is 18th from the front and 35th from the back. How many people are in the queue?

solutions.title: Count in front and behind
solutions.body:
There are $17$ people in front of Jess and $34$ behind her. With Jess herself: $17+1+34=52$.

**Answer: 52**

solutions.title: Overlap
solutions.body:
Counting from the front to Jess gives 18 people and from the back to Jess gives 35 people; Jess is counted twice, so $18+35-1=52$.

**Answer: 52**

prompt: $p$, $q$ and $r$ represent the numbers $2$, $3$, $4$ in some order. What is the greatest possible value of $p^q\times r$?

solutions.title: Try the orders
solutions.body:
The six values of $p^q r$ are $2^3\cdot4=32$, $2^4\cdot3=48$, $3^2\cdot4=36$, $3^4\cdot2=162$, $4^2\cdot3=48$, $4^3\cdot2=128$. The largest is $162$.

**Answer: 162**

prompt: $ABCDE$ is a regular pentagon with an exterior angle of $72^\circ$. What is the size of the angle marked $x$, in degrees?

solutions.title: Isosceles triangle
solutions.body:
Each interior angle of the pentagon is $180^\circ-72^\circ=108^\circ$. Triangle $BCD$ has $BC=CD$, so it is isosceles with apex angle $\angle BCD=108^\circ$ and $x=\frac12(180^\circ-108^\circ)=36^\circ$.

**Answer: 36**

prompt: The beginning of a sequence of expanding grids is shown. Case 3 has a grey central area of $9$ square units and a white border of $16$ square units. If the pattern of squares continues in the same way, how many white squares will there be in Case 10?

solutions.title: Subtract grey from total
solutions.body:
Case $n$ is an $(n+2)\times(n+2)$ grid whose central $n\times n$ block is grey. White squares: $(n+2)^2-n^2=4n+4$. For $n=10$ this is $44$.

**Answer: 44**

solutions.title: Count the border
solutions.body:
Case 10 has a $10\times10$ grey centre. The white border has two strips of $10$ (top and bottom) and two strips of $12$ (left and right, including corners): $20+24=44$.

**Answer: 44**

solutions.title: Pair the terms
solutions.body:
Pair each even number with the odd number just before it: $(2-1)+(4-3)+\dots+(200-199)$. There are $100$ pairs, each equal to $1$, so the total is $100$.

**Answer: 100**

prompt: The diagram shows a square inside an equilateral triangle. What is the value of $x+y$?

solutions.title: Angle sums
solutions.body:
The square has one vertex on the base. The angles between the base and the two sides of the square at that vertex are $a$ and $b$, and $a+b=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ$. The two base angles of the equilateral triangle are $60^\circ$. The two small triangles at the base corners have angle sums $x+a+60=180$ and $y+b+60=180$. Adding: $x+y+(a+b)=240$, so $x+y=240-90=150$.

**Answer: 150**

prompt: If the product of four consecutive integers is equal to the value of one of those integers, then what is the largest possible value for any of the integers?

solutions.title: Zero must be included
solutions.body:
Suppose none of the four integers is $0$ and the product equals one of them, $m$. Dividing by $m$, the other three integers (distinct and nonzero) would have product $1$, which would force all three to be $\pm1$, impossible. So one of the integers is $0$; then the product is $0$, which equals that integer. The possible quadruples are $-3,\dots,0$; $-2,\dots,1$; $-1,\dots,2$; $0,\dots,3$. The largest integer that can occur is $3$.

**Answer: 3**

prompt: What is the difference between the largest and the second largest odd factors of $2016$?

solutions.title: Factorise
solutions.body:
$2016=2^5\cdot3^2\cdot7$. Odd factors are the factors of $3^2\cdot7=63$. The largest is $63$, the second largest is $63/3=21$. Difference $=42$.

**Answer: 42**

prompt: There are twice as many girls as boys at a school. If $30\%$ of the girls and $45\%$ of the boys have already completed their holiday project, what percentage of the learners still needs to complete their project?

solutions.title: Pick a convenient number
solutions.body:
Take $200$ girls and $100$ boys. Completed: $60+45=105$ of $300$. Still to do: $195$ of $300=65\%$.

**Answer: 65**

solutions.title: Weighted average
solutions.body:
Completed fraction $=\frac23\cdot30\%+\frac13\cdot45\%=20\%+15\%=35\%$, so $65\%$ remain.

**Answer: 65**

prompt: In the figure, $ABCD$ is a rectangle. The area of triangle $DEC$ is $9\text{ cm}^2$ and $BE=\frac25BC$. What is the area of $ABCD$ in $\text{cm}^2$?

solutions.title: Use the base EC
solutions.body:
$EC=\frac35BC$. Triangle $DEC$ has base $EC$ and height $DC$, so its area is $\frac12\cdot\frac35BC\cdot DC=\frac3{10}[ABCD]=9$. Hence $[ABCD]=30$.

**Answer: 30**

prompt: Boris takes a taxi to his home but falls asleep when the taxi is halfway to his house. He wakes up when the remaining part of his journey is equal to half the distance covered by the taxi while he was asleep. If the fraction of the journey for which he slept is $\frac1n$, what is the value of $n$?

solutions.title: Units
solutions.body:
Let the remaining distance be $1$ unit. He slept for $2$ units. After waking he still has $1$ unit; he had been awake for half the journey, so $2+1=3$ units are the second half and the whole journey is $6$ units. He slept $\frac26=\frac13$ of the journey, so $n=3$.

**Answer: 3**

prompt: I accidentally decreased a number by $60\%$ instead of increasing it by $60\%$. This incorrect value now needs to be increased by $k\%$ to get to the correct value. What is the value of $k$?

solutions.title: Compare with the number
solutions.body:
I got $40\%$ of the number instead of $160\%$. To go from $40\%$ to $160\%$ I multiply by $4$, i.e. an increase of $300\%$.

**Answer: 300**

prompt: Exactly two years ago the Benson family had $4$ members, and their average age was $19$. The Bensons then adopted another child. If the average age of the family today is still $19$, what is the present age of the adopted child?

solutions.title: Total ages
solutions.body:
Two years ago the ages summed to $4\times19=76$. The four members have gained $2$ years each: $76+8=84$ now. With the child the sum is $5\times19=95$. The child is $95-84=11$.

**Answer: 11**

prompt: Four teams, $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ each play a single game against each of the other teams. There are no draws and teams $A$, $B$ and $C$ have the same number of wins. If team $A$ beats team $D$, how many wins does team $D$ have?

solutions.title: Count the wins
solutions.body:
There are $\binom42=6$ games, so $6$ wins in total. Let $A,B,C$ each have $w$ wins and $D$ have $d$ wins: $3w+d=6$. Since $A$ beat $D$, $d\le2$, so $d=0$ with $w=2$ (the only possibility, because $d\in\{0,3,6\}$ for $3w+d=6$ and $d\le 2$). An example: $A$ beats $B,D$; $B$ beats $C,D$; $C$ beats $A,D$.

**Answer: 0**

prompt: For how many positive integers $n$ less than $50$ is the product $(n-8)(n-38)$ positive?

solutions.title: Both factors same sign
solutions.body:
The product is positive when both factors are positive ($n>38$) or both negative ($n<8$). $n=1,\dots,7$ gives $7$ values and $n=39,\dots,49$ gives $11$ values. Total $18$.

**Answer: 18**

prompt: An equilateral triangle $ABC$ is shown alongside. The centre $G$ is joined to $A$, $B$ and $C$ forming three identical triangles. $D$, $E$ and $F$ are the midpoints of $AB$, $AC$ and $BC$ respectively. If the area of $\triangle ABC$ is $120\text{ cm}^2$, what is the shaded area in $\text{cm}^2$?

solutions.title: Split the shaded region
solutions.body:
The midpoints cut $ABC$ into four equal triangles. The line $AG$ passes through the midpoint $H$ of $DE$, so the part of the shaded region inside $ADE$ is triangle $AHE$, half of $ADE$: $\frac12\cdot\frac14=\frac18$ of $ABC$.

The rest of the shaded region lies inside triangle $DEF$, whose centre is also $G$. The lines $GA$, $GB$, $GC$ pass through the midpoints of the sides of $DEF$ and cut it into three congruent quadrilaterals; the shaded part $EHGI$ is one of them, so it is $\frac13\cdot\frac14=\frac1{12}$ of $ABC$.

Total: $\frac18+\frac1{12}=\frac5{24}$ of $120$, which is $25$.

**Answer: 25**

prompt: $AC$ and $BD$ are diameters of the circle. $AC=BD=6$ cm. If the area of the shaded region is $7\pi\text{ cm}^2$, find the value of $x$.

solutions.title: Fraction of the circle
solutions.body:
The radius is $3$ cm, so the circle has area $9\pi$. The unshaded area is $9\pi-7\pi=2\pi$, which is $\frac29$ of the circle. The unshaded regions are the two equal sectors at the top left and bottom right, so each has a central angle of $\frac12\cdot\frac29\cdot360^\circ=40^\circ$.

The triangle formed by the centre $O$, $B$ and $C$ is isosceles ($OB=OC$) with apex angle $40^\circ$, so $x=\frac{180^\circ-40^\circ}2=70^\circ$.

**Answer: 70**

prompt: For how many positive three-digit numbers is the hundreds digit smaller than the units digit?

solutions.title: Count by hundreds and units
solutions.body:
Choose the hundreds digit $h\in\{1,\dots,9\}$ and units digit $u>h$: there are $9-h$ choices for $u$, and the tens digit is free ($10$ choices). Total: $10\sum_{h=1}^{9}(9-h)=10(8+7+\dots+0)=10\cdot36=360$.

**Answer: 360**
